unmapped_findings: Precipitation strengthening (Ashby-Orowan, eq. 1) reported for the annealed alloy system, not specifically A15: IG-B2 (0.29 μm, 1.1%) in RE-γ (Figure 3a) gives 23 MPa; IG-B2 (0.2 μm, 2.6%) in URE-γ gives 43 MPa; total IG-B2 strengthening = 66 MPa (b0025-b0026, b0040).

Interrupted-tensile TEM/EBSD of 'A15' at engineering strain e = 0.05 (Figure 7c-e): higher dislocation density in γ than in B2; GND localization at γ/B2 interfaces. Route attribution ambiguous - Figure 7 appears in the modified-HR discussion, so this 'A15' may be the modified-route A15 rather than the standard-route A15.

B2 stringer bands reported present up to 16% in the annealed sample microstructure (b0041); the modified route reduced stringer band fraction from 16% to 11% (b0032). No per-sample stringer fraction is given for standard-route A15.

The abstract-level final outcome (nearly 1 GPa yield strength, 28% total elongation, >1.7 kJ/mol or 238.4 J/cm^3 toughness) refers to the improved modified-route steel, not to the standard-route A15 sample.

A15 fracture surface (Figure 4 upper panel) is annotated 'void nucleation' and 'B2 stringer', consistent with the general finding that macrovoids nucleate inside B2 stringer bands and cause premature failure (b0030, b0043).
